docs.text: Bake Layer Data to Blender Native ¶ Click Current Bind Mesh to open a dropdown list showing all bind meshes in the scene. The model's layers have been initialized with Super Skin Pro. The model's layers have been initialized with Super Skin Pro, but it is missing the Armature modifier. The model uses native Blender data. Click Bake Selected or Bake All to bake the layer results back to native Blender weights. Baking Merges Layers Once baked, all layers will be merged. To keep them, export the weights first, or don't bake. You can still share the unbaked file with anyone, even if they don't have this add-on. Editing Without Baking If you continue skinning using native Blender without baking, returning to the add-on tools will overwrite your changes with the last saved add-on state.
docs.title: Bake to Blender Native

docs.text: FAQ (Frequently Asked Questions) ¶ Learning the Add-on ¶ I've never done layer-based weight painting before. What can it do? Think of it like Photoshop layers, but for skin weights. You can fix parts without breaking your old work, mix weights together, or even paint weights from scratch. Where should I start learning the layer-based workflow? We recommend starting with our YouTube Tutorial Playlist . If you want to read more details, check out our User Guide . Add-on Compatibility ¶ Does this add-on work with any rig? Yes, absolutely. The add-on only paints weights and doesn't change your rig. You can use it with any rig, including custom rigs, Rigify, or Auto-Rig Pro. Will my skin weights work for people who don't have this add-on? Yes. Other people can open and use your .blend files normally, even if they don't have this add-on. Are future updates free? Yes, updates are free for life. Buy it once, and all future updates (bug fixes and new tools) are free to download from your Gumroad Library. If I update to a newer version, will my older files still work? Yes. Old files will still work fine. Updating the add-on will not break or change your saved weights. Does the add-on support custom shortcuts? Yes. Go to the add-on panel, then click Settings > Edit Shortcuts . Which Blender versions does the add-on support? The add-on supports Blender 4.2 and newer, including 4.5, 5.0, 5.1, and 5.2. Support & Community ¶ How do I get help or report bugs? Join the Super Skin Pro Discord Server to chat, ask questions, or report bugs. Are there any plans for new features? Do you accept feature requests? Yes! Right now, my main goal is fixing bugs and making sure everything runs smoothly. But I'm always happy to hear your ideas! I will check every request to see if it helps most users. Feel free to share your thoughts in our Super Skin Pro Discord Server . Add-on Limitations ¶ Blender's Native Skinning Tools Please use the add-on's own tools (Mirror, Transfer, Smooth/Brush, and Vertex Selection) instead of Blender's default tools while working with layers. Watch the Brush & Vertex Selection tutorial . Baking to Native Blender You can bake your weights back to normal Blender anytime: Baking Documentation (Note: baking merges all layers together). To keep things easy to edit, we recommend keeping your layers until your project is finished. Modifier Stack Order When skinning, try not to put heavy deformation modifiers above the Armature modifier in the list.
docs.title: FAQ

docs.text: Drag-and-Drop Installation ¶ Download the SuperSkinPro .zip file from Gumroad . Open Blender , drag and drop the .zip file directly into the Blender viewport/window, and confirm the installation. Restart Blender after installing or updating the add-on. Once installed, SuperSkinPro will appear in the N-Panel sidebar. Always Restart Blender After Updating or Reinstalling If you update or reinstall the add-on, you must always restart Blender afterward to ensure the add-on works properly. How to Update ¶ When a new update is released, you can re-download the latest SuperSkinPro files from your Gumroad Library and repeat the installation steps above.

docs.text: Keep Volume ¶ When Keep Volume is enabled, it automatically maintains mesh distance and seamlessly connects separated seams. Ideal for clothing or multi-part meshes. Keep Volume works in all modes—whether you are using brush paint, vertex selection, or clicking flood weight from the N-panel. When Keep Volume is enabled in vertex mode, you can select vertices across connected seams as if they were a single mesh.

docs.text: Mirror Weight ¶ Target Side: The side that receives the mirrored weights. The blue plane in the viewport HUD marks the target side. Mirror Target Data: Mirror only the Layer Mask, only the Bone Weight, or both (the default). Use Custom Keywords (Optional): Add your own left and right keywords for rigs with non-standard bone names. Most users never need this. Mirror All Layers: On by default, so Mirror Weight affects every layer. Turn it off to mirror only the layer selected in the Layer List. Mirror to Selected Vertices If vertices are selected, only those vertices are mirrored. Auto Mirror Weight ¶ When Auto Mirror is on, every weight change is mirrored to the other side automatically, whether it comes from the brush, vertex selection, Block Weight , Self Transfer or Hammer Weight .

docs.text: Object Mode Tools ¶ Weight Transfer ¶ Weight transfer supports any number of source and target meshes. It can be used in various ways, such as: 1) Transfer weights from the body to clothing and accessories ¶ How to use: Add both the body and clothing to the Transfer list. Mark the body mesh as Source . Click Transfer Weight . 2) Transfer weights from multiple meshes ¶ How to use: Add the source meshes and the target mesh to the Transfer list. Mark the relevant meshes as Source . Click Transfer Weight . 3) And much more, as shown in the video ¶ Other Transfer Options: You can restrict the transfer to specific source or target areas by enabling the Use Selected Vertices Only toggle (the selection must exist in Edit Mode). A source selection can be faces, edges, or single vertices. If the target already has a layer system, the output will be added as a new layer named "Transfer Output". Enabling the Force Target to Init Layer checkbox forces layer data initialization for all target meshes if they are still using native vertex groups. Armature Parenting Target meshes do not need to be parented to an armature beforehand, as the tool will automatically parent them during the transfer. However, the source mesh must always be parented to an armature first . Weight Export ¶ Export all layer data and skin weights from a selected mesh to a file. How to use: Select the mesh you want to export layer data from. Click Export Weights . Weight Import ¶ How to use: Select the target mesh you want to import weights to. Click Import Weights . Options: Transfer Method: Choose a weight transfer method during import, such as Closest Distance or Vertex ID . Preserve Existing Layers: Check this option to keep current layers on the mesh. (This option only appears if the target mesh already has layer data.)
docs.title: Object Mode Tools

docs.text: Quick Start ¶ If this is your first time using Super Skin Pro, follow these steps to get started with the add-on. 1) Parent Mesh to Rig ¶ Make sure your model is parented to an armature. In Object Mode, select your model and then the armature, and press Ctrl + P to parent the model to the armature. Choose With Empty Groups if you want to start skin weights from scratch. Choose With Automatic Weights if you want to continue from automatic weights. After parenting, an Armature modifier appears and vertex groups are created, which means you are ready for the next step: weight painting. 2) Open Super Skin Pro via the N-Panel ¶ Press N in the viewport to show the N-Panel sidebar, then go to the "Super Skin Pro" tab. Select your character mesh. You can switch between 4 modes: 1) Object Mode 2) Weight Paint Mode with Brush Painting 3) Weight Paint Mode with Vertex Selection 4) Pose Mode 3) Basic Bone Selection & Block Weight ¶ This tutorial shows how to select bones in the viewport and how to use the Block Weight tool. 4) Paint Weights with Brush & Vertex Selection ¶ Learn how to paint weights with the brush and with vertex selection. 5) Learn More ¶ Now that you know the basics of the add-on, pick the tutorials that match your workflow. Use Layers to Fix Existing Weights ¶ Paint Body Weights with Layers from Scratch ¶ Paint Facial Weights with Layers from Scratch ¶ Watch More Tutorials on YouTube ¶ Read the Full User Guide ¶

docs.text: 1.3.1 ¶ 1.3.1 Fixed: The mesh no longer shifts while painting on rigs with scaled bones and Preserve Volume on. 1.3.0 ( Minor Update ) ¶ 1.3.0 ( Minor Update ) Performance Improvements ¶ The add-on is much faster when entering Weight Paint Mode and when skinning high-poly meshes. Auto Mirror ¶ Added Auto Mirror. When turned on, any change you make (with the brush, vertex selection, Block Weight, Self Transfer, or Hammer Weight) automatically mirrors to the other side. Hammer Weight Improvement ¶ Hammer Weight now lists the layers causing the problem. This makes fixing weights much easier, no matter which layer you're currently on. Note Removed the Blend option from Hammer Weight, as the tool is meant for quickly fixing weight leaks. Settings Improvement ¶ Overhauled the settings popup into separate tabs, making it easier to configure each part of the add-on. The Shortcut Settings menu has been redesigned. You can now easily view all available shortcuts organized by category. You can now customize the viewport colors in Weight Paint Mode, including the wireframe and the color gradients for bone and mask weights. Other Fixes ¶ Improved the active mesh display in Weight Paint Mode: it is always drawn in front, so you no longer need to isolate it. Improved switching from Vertex Selection Mode to Brush Mode: a minimum set of faces stays visible even when only a single vertex is selected. Improved Keep Volume to better retain internal mesh volume and thickness while reducing the ping-pong effect. Improved the button labels and icons in the vertex selection popup to make them easier to read. Improved skin weight preservation after applying topology-changing modifiers such as Subdivision, matching native Blender behavior. Added support for selecting triangulated meshes in Vertex Selection Mode. Transfer Weight now supports selecting individual source vertices without requiring full faces. Improved Mirror Weight to follow mesh topology more accurately across sides, even on non-symmetrical geometry. Improved Weight Paint viewport stability when extra deformation modifiers follow the Armature modifier. For accurate results, we still recommend disabling modifiers such as Subdivision or Solidify while painting. 1.2.3 ¶ 1.2.3 Fixed: "Smooth Affected Only" had no effect on a full selection and could spread weight further on a partial one. Smooth now keeps empty vertices empty and adds no new bones to a vertex. 1.2.2 ¶ 1.2.2 Surface Brush ¶ Improved: Surface Brush: Automatically isolates front and back surfaces to prevent weight bleeding while brushing. Keep Volume ¶ Improved: Resolved depth conflicts so the innermost layer always leads and layers never swap roles, preventing the ping-pong effect. Improved: "Connected Only" option now maintains Keep Volume independently per piece. Changed: Brushes and selections now strictly affect vertices within their bounds. Fixed: Sharpen Weight brush no longer breaks seam welds when Keep Volume is enabled. Others ¶ Improved: "Mirror All Layers" and "Always Show Bone HUD" settings now save app-wide (Preferences). Improved: "Front Face Only (Lasso)", "Sync with Edit Mode Selection", "Move Weight by Name", and "Limit Total's Max Influences" settings now save per scene in the .blend file. 1.2.1 ¶ 1.2.1 Added: "Sync with Edit Mode Selection" in Vertex Mode header to share selection and hidden vertices with Edit Mode. Improved: Deform bone selection sync across Pose Mode and Weight Paint. Improved: Independent Strength Pressure for Surface (On by default) and Projected brushes (Off by default). Fixed: Resolved shortcut conflicts with native Blender tools—now restricted to Brush and Vertex modes. 1.2.0 ( Minor Update ) ¶ 1.2.0 ( Minor Update ) Brush Paint Update ¶ - Falloff Preset ¶ You can now change the falloff type for surface brush and projected brush. There are 3 presets: constant, smooth, and linear. Removed Options Old falloff pressure and falloff sliders have been removed. Removed size pressure since strength pressure is usually enough for weight painting. - Connected Only Option for Brush ¶ You can now check the "Connected Only" option. This limits your weight painting to only affect the connected surface parts. - Support Off-Mesh Painting when using Surface Brush ¶ Surface brush can now be used even when the brush cursor is outside the mesh. This makes fine-tuning silhouettes much easier. - Brush HUD Color Customization ¶ Now you can change cursor colors in the cursor dropdown menu. Enhanced Sharpen Weight ¶ Sharpen Weight has been heavily improved. New Behavior: Keep Volume ¶ - Easily Paint Weights on Clothes! ¶ When Keep Volume is on, it automatically keeps mesh distance and connects separated seams nicely. - Supports both Brush and Vertex modes ¶ Keep Volume works in all modes—whether you are using brush paint, vertex selection, or clicking flood weight from the N-panel. - Keep Separate Surface Selection as One ¶ When Keep Volume is enabled, you can select vertices across connected seams as if they were a single mesh. UX & UI Improvements ¶ - Update Behavior Across Vertex Selection and Brush Mode ¶ Hammer Weight, Self Transfer, and Copy Vertex Weight now only show up in Vertex Mode. If you have a vertex selection and switch to brush mode, it will automatically isolate the selected area. Note To keep things clean, we removed add vertex selection, remove selection, and hide/unhide mesh features from brush mode. Those tasks now belong fully to vertex mode. - Weight Steps ¶ Added step buttons for sliders in the N-panel. Use weight step buttons to smoothly increase or decrease weight values. This makes weights easier to control and perfectly fits the feel of each weight operation. - Refine Slider Pop-up UI ¶ Brush Mode - Right Click Popup Weight Slider Vertex Mode - Right Click Popup Weight Slider - Select Multiple Bones Faster with Lasso ¶ Click and drag around the bones to automatically use lasso selection. - Add Bone HUD Color Customization ¶ You can now set the color of the Bone HUD. - Add Mirror to All Layers Option ¶ Added a "mirror to all layers" option. Since most characters are symmetrical, turning this on ensures you never forget to mirror other layers and saves time from having to select every layer manually. - Add Show Shortcut Hint Option ¶ You can now toggle shortcut hints on and off through the add-on settings button. Other Improvements ¶ Improved smooth weight to work much better on dense topology meshes without needing overly high smooth settings. Improved the block weight algorithm for the face ring option. Improved the UI so self-transfer is easier to use without needing to toggle out to set a new source. Improved camera rotation to be easier to control. Improved mirror weight performance. Removed smooth and repeat options from block weight since they duplicated the regular smooth buttons in the N-panel. Fixed a bug where block weight popups could not edit past values if a bone was selected after using block weight. Fixed the right-click popup in brush and vertex modes where settings would close immediately after changing them. Fixed shortcut bugs where add-on shortcuts leaked into native Blender weight paint mode. Fixed vertex weight operation gestures to be more compatible with pen tablets. Prevented native brush settings popups from showing up when pressing Alt+F, Shift+F, or Ctrl+F. 1.1.7 ¶ 1.1.7 Fixed: While weight painting, orbiting now rotates around the bone you last selected or the spot you last painted. Fixed: The Bake popup is shorter and narrower, with a Bake button instead of OK. Improved viewport orbiting around selection in v1.1.7 1.1.6 ¶ 1.1.6 Fixed: with Orbit Around Selection turned on, orbiting during weight painting rotated around the character’s origin. It now rotates around the view center. 1.1.5 ¶ 1.1.5 Fixed: Pressing Numpad . during Weight Paint mode now centers the view on the mesh weighted to the active bone, allowing orbiting directly around that bone. Fixed: The Bone HUD skeleton is now rendered beneath the viewport HUD text to keep the text readable. 1.1.4 ¶ 1.1.4 Fixed: Importing weights no longer opens the file browser a second time after the import completes. Import now opens the file browser directly. Import settings (Method, Preserve Existing Layers) are in an Options section of the file browser's side panel. Import and Export are only enabled when a mesh is selected in the viewport. Export also requires the mesh to contain layer data. 1.1.3 ¶ 1.1.3 Add, Scale and Smooth now show a warning in the status bar when weight could not be distributed or pulled from other bones, or when Smooth found nothing to change, with a hint that some bones may be locked. Edit Weight Mode now shows how many vertices are hidden at the bottom of the viewport until they are revealed. The Deform Bones list is now locked outside Edit Weight Mode and can only be used while editing weights. Select Locked and Select Unlocked now show a message when no bone matches. Fixed Select Locked and Select Unlocked clearing the current bone selection when no bone matched. Fixed the add-on panel shifting up slightly when switching to Pose Mode. 1.1.2 ¶ 1.1.2 Improved the toast HUD for the Limit Total, Normalize, and Selection tools. Fixed the "Weight brush not found" warning when entering Weight Paint mode. Added a documentation link to the add-on manifest and removed the Gumroad link button from the UI. 1.1.1 ¶ 1.1.1 Restored the "Preserve Existing Layers" option in the Import Weight dialog. 1.1.0 ( Minor Update ) ¶ 1.1.0 ( Minor Update ) Mirror Weight Settings Update ¶ Since Blender mostly mirrors along the X-axis anyway, we made the mirror weight options simpler. Added a target side HUD preview: the blue plane area shows the target side for mirroring. The "Use Custom Keywords" option is now an optional setting, intended only for users who use keywords that differ greatly from the standard ones. General users no longer need to configure this. Bone HUD Update ¶ Improved the Bone HUD display to make it easier to see. Added an option for "Always show bone display" to keep the Bone HUD visible all the time, located in the More Button next to the Deform Bone List (enabled by default). Moved the option for adjusting Bone Size into the More Button of the Deform Bone List as well. Selection Update ¶ Added options to select unaffected vertices / deselect unaffected vertices for greater flexibility in use. Other Bug Fixes and Improvements ¶ We improved the Transfer Weight options and behavior to make them easier to understand. You can read more in Weight Transfer . The Transfer Weight list and Active Mesh list now support selecting multiple items at once. Improved the system so it can smooth between existing bone weights and empty weight areas. Now supports Apple M-Series. The popup width now auto-sizes to fit the item names. Improved icons to clearly distinguish between meshes using layer-based skin weights and native weights. 1.0.13 ¶ 1.0.13 Weight Transfer fix: when “Use Selected Vertices Only” is on for the source, the mask is now taken from the same selected area as the weight. Before, it could come from the nearest unselected area. Improved the mask color to make it clearer. Fixed a Deform Bone List weight color display error when the armature has no deform bones. 1.0.12 ¶ 1.0.12 Improved performance when applying weights. Fixed skin weights breaking after editing meshes. 1.0.11 ¶ 1.0.11 Entering Blender's native Weight Paint Mode no longer forces the add-on mode, preserving standard workflows for non-deform vertex groups. 1.0.10 ¶ 1.0.10 Added a status for meshes with layer data but missing an Armature modifier. Added pressure sensitivity toggles for brush size, hardness, and strength. Added a Normalize Weights button to the Limit Total popup. Increased the maximum brush size limit for surface brushes. Fixed an issue where applying weights affected non-deform vertex groups. (Crucial Bug) 1.0.9 ¶ 1.0.9 Added a button to switch to Object Mode. Added a fade-out effect when exiting Bone Picker. Added a Clear button to the Transfer Settings popup. Improved add-on performance when switching layers and smoothing weights. Fixed Armature not hiding when entering Weight Paint mode. Fixed a weight smoothing error at extreme values. 1.0.8 ¶ 1.0.8 Major UI redesign. Added shortcut customization to the Settings button. Added new features: "Set Total" (limit max bone influences) and "Hammer" (average vertex weights). Removed auto-update feature. Improved add-on performance. 1.0.7 ¶ 1.0.7 Improved the bind mesh dropdown in the List Viewer to be easier to use — see Clean-up Layer Data for details. Improved the Weight Transfer interface to be easier to use. 1.0.6 ¶ 1.0.6 Shortcut Guide: Press Alt + 4 while editing to toggle the Shortcut Guide. Mask Edit Toggle: Press Alt + 1 while editing to toggle Mask Edit mode. Selection Persistence: Exiting Mask Edit mode now preserves all active selections in the Deform Bone list. Repeat Last Operation: Added support for Shift + R to repeat the most recent Apply Weight operation. UI Improvements: Enhanced the user interface for both the Layer List and Deform Bone List sections. Bug Fixes: Multi-Color Mode: Fixed display updates to ensure higher accuracy when using Mirror Weight and Auto Assign Weight. Scale Weight Distribution: Improved the scaling behavior to distribute weight more intelligently based on the rig hierarchy. 1.0.5 ¶ 1.0.5 Bone Picker now shows a header text indicating that bone picking mode is active. Bone Picker now displays the name of the hovered bone. Bone Picker has a redesigned color scheme for showing bone selection status. Improved performance when hovering bones with Multi Color mode enabled. Extended add-on support to Blender 4.2 LTS and newer. Bug Fixes: Fixed the Viewport Overlay not being restored when exiting Edit Weight mode back to the user's normal edit mode. Fixed the Initialize system running again automatically when selecting a mesh.

docs.text: 1.3.1 Fixed: The mesh no longer shifts while painting on rigs with scaled bones and Preserve Volume on.
1.3.0 ( Minor Update )
docs.title: 1.3.0 ( Minor Update )

docs.text: The add-on is much faster when entering Weight Paint Mode and when skinning high-poly meshes.
docs.title: Performance Improvements

docs.text: Added Auto Mirror. When turned on, any change you make (with the brush, vertex selection, Block Weight, Self Transfer, or Hammer Weight) automatically mirrors to the other side.
docs.title: Auto Mirror

docs.text: Hammer Weight now lists the layers causing the problem. This makes fixing weights much easier, no matter which layer you're currently on. Note Removed the Blend option from Hammer Weight, as the tool is meant for quickly fixing weight leaks.
docs.title: Hammer Weight Improvement

docs.text: Overhauled the settings popup into separate tabs, making it easier to configure each part of the add-on. The Shortcut Settings menu has been redesigned. You can now easily view all available shortcuts organized by category. You can now customize the viewport colors in Weight Paint Mode, including the wireframe and the color gradients for bone and mask weights.
docs.title: Settings Improvement

docs.text: Improved the active mesh display in Weight Paint Mode: it is always drawn in front, so you no longer need to isolate it. Improved switching from Vertex Selection Mode to Brush Mode: a minimum set of faces stays visible even when only a single vertex is selected. Improved Keep Volume to better retain internal mesh volume and thickness while reducing the ping-pong effect. Improved the button labels and icons in the vertex selection popup to make them easier to read. Improved skin weight preservation after applying topology-changing modifiers such as Subdivision, matching native Blender behavior. Added support for selecting triangulated meshes in Vertex Selection Mode. Transfer Weight now supports selecting individual source vertices without requiring full faces. Improved Mirror Weight to follow mesh topology more accurately across sides, even on non-symmetrical geometry. Improved Weight Paint viewport stability when extra deformation modifiers follow the Armature modifier. For accurate results, we still recommend disabling modifiers such as Subdivision or Solidify while painting.
docs.title: Other Fixes

docs.text: 1.2.3 Fixed: "Smooth Affected Only" had no effect on a full selection and could spread weight further on a partial one. Smooth now keeps empty vertices empty and adds no new bones to a vertex.
Improved: Surface Brush: Automatically isolates front and back surfaces to prevent weight bleeding while brushing.
docs.title: Surface Brush

docs.text: Improved: Resolved depth conflicts so the innermost layer always leads and layers never swap roles, preventing the ping-pong effect. Improved: "Connected Only" option now maintains Keep Volume independently per piece. Changed: Brushes and selections now strictly affect vertices within their bounds. Fixed: Sharpen Weight brush no longer breaks seam welds when Keep Volume is enabled.
docs.title: Keep Volume

docs.text: Improved: "Mirror All Layers" and "Always Show Bone HUD" settings now save app-wide (Preferences). Improved: "Front Face Only (Lasso)", "Sync with Edit Mode Selection", "Move Weight by Name", and "Limit Total's Max Influences" settings now save per scene in the .blend file.
docs.title: Others

docs.text: 1.2.1 Added: "Sync with Edit Mode Selection" in Vertex Mode header to share selection and hidden vertices with Edit Mode. Improved: Deform bone selection sync across Pose Mode and Weight Paint. Improved: Independent Strength Pressure for Surface (On by default) and Projected brushes (Off by default). Fixed: Resolved shortcut conflicts with native Blender tools—now restricted to Brush and Vertex modes.
1.2.0 ( Minor Update )
docs.title: 1.2.0 ( Minor Update )

docs.text: You can now change the falloff type for surface brush and projected brush. There are 3 presets: constant, smooth, and linear. Removed Options Old falloff pressure and falloff sliders have been removed. Removed size pressure since strength pressure is usually enough for weight painting.
docs.title: - Falloff Preset

docs.text: You can now check the "Connected Only" option. This limits your weight painting to only affect the connected surface parts.
docs.title: - Connected Only Option for Brush

docs.text: Surface brush can now be used even when the brush cursor is outside the mesh. This makes fine-tuning silhouettes much easier.
docs.title: - Support Off-Mesh Painting when using Surface Brush

docs.text: Now you can change cursor colors in the cursor dropdown menu.
docs.title: - Brush HUD Color Customization

docs.text: Sharpen Weight has been heavily improved.
docs.title: Enhanced Sharpen Weight

docs.text: When Keep Volume is on, it automatically keeps mesh distance and connects separated seams nicely.
docs.title: - Easily Paint Weights on Clothes!

docs.text: Keep Volume works in all modes—whether you are using brush paint, vertex selection, or clicking flood weight from the N-panel.
docs.title: - Supports both Brush and Vertex modes

docs.text: When Keep Volume is enabled, you can select vertices across connected seams as if they were a single mesh.
docs.title: - Keep Separate Surface Selection as One

docs.text: Hammer Weight, Self Transfer, and Copy Vertex Weight now only show up in Vertex Mode. If you have a vertex selection and switch to brush mode, it will automatically isolate the selected area. Note To keep things clean, we removed add vertex selection, remove selection, and hide/unhide mesh features from brush mode. Those tasks now belong fully to vertex mode.
docs.title: - Update Behavior Across Vertex Selection and Brush Mode

docs.text: Added step buttons for sliders in the N-panel. Use weight step buttons to smoothly increase or decrease weight values. This makes weights easier to control and perfectly fits the feel of each weight operation.
docs.title: - Weight Steps

docs.text: Brush Mode - Right Click Popup Weight Slider Vertex Mode - Right Click Popup Weight Slider
docs.title: - Refine Slider Pop-up UI

docs.text: Click and drag around the bones to automatically use lasso selection.
docs.title: - Select Multiple Bones Faster with Lasso

docs.text: You can now set the color of the Bone HUD.
docs.title: - Add Bone HUD Color Customization

docs.text: Added a "mirror to all layers" option. Since most characters are symmetrical, turning this on ensures you never forget to mirror other layers and saves time from having to select every layer manually.
docs.title: - Add Mirror to All Layers Option

docs.text: You can now toggle shortcut hints on and off through the add-on settings button.
docs.title: - Add Show Shortcut Hint Option

docs.text: Improved smooth weight to work much better on dense topology meshes without needing overly high smooth settings. Improved the block weight algorithm for the face ring option. Improved the UI so self-transfer is easier to use without needing to toggle out to set a new source. Improved camera rotation to be easier to control. Improved mirror weight performance. Removed smooth and repeat options from block weight since they duplicated the regular smooth buttons in the N-panel. Fixed a bug where block weight popups could not edit past values if a bone was selected after using block weight. Fixed the right-click popup in brush and vertex modes where settings would close immediately after changing them. Fixed shortcut bugs where add-on shortcuts leaked into native Blender weight paint mode. Fixed vertex weight operation gestures to be more compatible with pen tablets. Prevented native brush settings popups from showing up when pressing Alt+F, Shift+F, or Ctrl+F.
docs.title: Other Improvements

docs.text: 1.1.7 Fixed: While weight painting, orbiting now rotates around the bone you last selected or the spot you last painted. Fixed: The Bake popup is shorter and narrower, with a Bake button instead of OK. Improved viewport orbiting around selection in v1.1.7
1.1.6 Fixed: with Orbit Around Selection turned on, orbiting during weight painting rotated around the character’s origin. It now rotates around the view center.

1.1.5 Fixed: Pressing Numpad . during Weight Paint mode now centers the view on the mesh weighted to the active bone, allowing orbiting directly around that bone. Fixed: The Bone HUD skeleton is now rendered beneath the viewport HUD text to keep the text readable.

1.1.4 Fixed: Importing weights no longer opens the file browser a second time after the import completes. Import now opens the file browser directly. Import settings (Method, Preserve Existing Layers) are in an Options section of the file browser's side panel. Import and Export are only enabled when a mesh is selected in the viewport. Export also requires the mesh to contain layer data.

1.1.3 Add, Scale and Smooth now show a warning in the status bar when weight could not be distributed or pulled from other bones, or when Smooth found nothing to change, with a hint that some bones may be locked. Edit Weight Mode now shows how many vertices are hidden at the bottom of the viewport until they are revealed. The Deform Bones list is now locked outside Edit Weight Mode and can only be used while editing weights. Select Locked and Select Unlocked now show a message when no bone matches. Fixed Select Locked and Select Unlocked clearing the current bone selection when no bone matched. Fixed the add-on panel shifting up slightly when switching to Pose Mode.

1.1.2 Improved the toast HUD for the Limit Total, Normalize, and Selection tools. Fixed the "Weight brush not found" warning when entering Weight Paint mode. Added a documentation link to the add-on manifest and removed the Gumroad link button from the UI.
1.1.1 Restored the "Preserve Existing Layers" option in the Import Weight dialog.

Self Transfer ¶ Transfers weight from one part of a mesh to another part of the same mesh: Select the vertices, edges or faces to use as the source, press Self Transfer... , then press Mark Source in the popup. Select the target vertices, press Self Transfer... again, then press Transfer in the popup. Transfer Target The transfer changes both the bone weights and the mask of the active layer.

docs.text: Interface Overview ¶ 1) Active Bind Mesh ¶ Shows the currently selected mesh. Click it to open a popup with the option to Bake Layer Data to Blender Native . 2) Layer List ¶ Displays all skin weight layers. You can add, delete, reorder, duplicate, merge, and toggle the visibility of each layer. Watch how to get started with layers or why you should use layers . Toggle Layer: Click the icon in front of a layer to turn it on or off. Rename Layer: Double-click the layer name to rename it. 3) Bone List ¶ Displays the active deform bones. Watch basic bone selection in Weight Paint Mode or read how to select bones in the viewport . Lock / Unlock: Click the lock icon in front of any bone to prevent weight bleeding . Focus Viewport: Double-click a bone to focus on it in the 3D viewport. Filter Influenced Bones: Toggle via the button in the right menu to display only bones with weights. Layer List & Bone List Shortcuts Both the bone and layer lists support the following shortcuts: Ctrl + Click : Add or remove items individually Shift + Click : Select a range of items Ctrl + A or Alt + Shift + Click : Select all items in the list Ctrl + I : Invert selection 4) Mode Switcher ¶ Switches between Object Mode, Brush Paint Mode, Vertex Selection Mode and Pose Mode. - How to Transfer, Export and Import Weights in Object Mode ¶ - Weight Paint Mode with Brush / Vertex Selection ¶

docs.text: Weight Operation ¶ Used for adjusting weights and quickly flooding values to selected areas. Add Weight Increases weight strength. Range: 0.001 – 1.0 Scale Weight Decreases weight by multiplying it (lower = reduces more, higher = reduces less). Range: 0.0 – 0.999 Smooth Weight Blends weights smoothly. Range: 0.001 – 1.0 (can go up to 100) Sharpen Weight Sharpens weight edges. Range: 0.001 – 1.0 Note If no vertices are selected, flooding will apply to the entire mesh. Use the weight step buttons to smoothly increase or decrease weight values. This makes weights easier to control and perfectly fits the feel of each weight operation. Multi-Color Preview ¶ Note While in Bone Mode, press Alt + 3 to toggle Multi-Color Preview. Multi-Color mode may impact performance.
